newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela National Guard may be removed from jails.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela National Guard may be removed from jails.

text.p: National guardsmen providing security at Venezuela's violence-prone jails may be removed following a prison fire apparently started by guards that killed 25 inmates, officials said on Friday.
Defence and Justice Ministry officials will meet to decide whether the national guard should continue to patrol jails after Tuesday's tragedy, Defence Minister Pedro Valencia said.

"If they (the national guard) are not wanted then that's absolutely no problem," Valencia told reporters. The guard has bolstered security at Venezuela's prisons for several years and 10 guardsmen on duty at the time of the fire at La Planta jail in southwest Caracas are under arrest, he said.
Justice Ministry officials have insisted that three national guardsmen were behind the tragedy.

"There's proof that these three guards locked the door, lobbed in tear gas canisters and that these set fire to the mattresses," Justice Minister Henrique Meier told Reuters late on Thursday. He said police tests showed that the tear gas canisters had created the sparks that started the fire.

Prisoners have said the fire began after an argument between inmates and guards during an early morning roll call. About 40 inmates were trapped inside the small cell. Some prisoners managed to crawl to safety through a small hole in the roof. The rest died engulfed in flames.

Valencia said it was important to prosecute those responsible, but he questioned the official line that the tear gas canisters had started the fire. "All I know is that a tear gas canister produces gas, not fire," he said.

Morgue officials said on Friday they had managed to identify 24 of the 25 charred and twisted bodies brought from the jail. Burns were so bad that many relatives have not been able to recognise their loved ones.

The National Prisons Director office said forensic tests found no traces of flammable liquids and corroborated the official line that the tear gas canisters had provided the spark that started the fire.
Venezuela's overcrowded and decaying prisons, considered to be among the most dangerous in Latin America, are frequent scenes of violence between inmates and clashes with guards.

The tragedy at La Planta was the worst in Venezuela's jails since about 120 prisoners were burned or hacked to death with machetes during a gang fight at the Sabaneta jail in the western city of Maracaibo in January 1994.
Converted from an army barracks more than 30 years ago to house 550 inmates, La Planta currently holds 1,700. About 70 percent of them have not been sentenced, officials said.
